page.layout: One page of text, one main column on the left of the scan with the running head and page number above it. To the right, below "EX.", a faint column of about seventeen lines in very light print that cannot be read. Outside the text block, the left margin holds only the binding and a pencilled shelf mark, which are not transcribed.

main_text.p: roni nostro cum Aristotele conueniat, in partiti-bus perorationis. nam Aristoteles ipse quatuor -ex partib.eam constare dicit:primum ex ea quæ efficit,ut auditor nobis bene velit,adversarijs ma-le:deinde ex amplificatione,&c diminutione:tum ex animorum comotione, ut afficiatur auditor : postremò ex enumeratione.sed facilis est recon-ciliatio.Tria illa priora,Ciceronis amplifica-ne continentur: nam illis tribus nihil aliud voluit Aristoteles,quàm varios mo-tus significare.

page.notes: The faint column to the right of and below "EX." is too light to read; its lines are marked illegible and only their approximate number is given. The "EX." is set apart on the line above that column and is copied as printed. The first word "roni" is a fragment of "Ciceroni" broken at the start of the page. The page number may read "129²" in the scan; it is given as 1292. Changes made: u/v and i/j normalised to the vowel or consonant form; long s written as plain s.
